name: The History of the Early Church (Acts)

objectives.text: Retell that Jesus went up to heaven and promised to send the Holy Spirit to his followers
Identify the sound of wind and the tongues of fire as signs that the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost
Name Peter and Paul as leaders in the early church who told others about Jesus
Recall that the church began in Jerusalem and describe how the first believers learned, prayed, ate together, and shared what they had
Summarize how the gospel spread from Jerusalem to Judea, Samaria, and the ends of the earth as Jesus said it would
Describe how the church chose seven men to care for widows so the apostles could keep preaching and praying
Explain what happened at Pentecost, including Peter's sermon and how the crowd responded
Describe how the Bereans examined the Scriptures and practice checking a teaching against a Bible passage in class
Compare Peter's boldness before the council after Pentecost with his fear when he denied Jesus
Retell the witness and death of Stephen and the ministry of Philip in Samaria and to the Ethiopian official
Describe the conversion and calling of Saul and explain how it changed the direction of his life
Trace Paul's missionary journeys and his voyage to Rome on a map of the Roman world
Construct a timeline of the major events in Acts from the Ascension to Paul's imprisonment in Rome
Analyze the conflict over circumcision and how the Jerusalem Council resolved it
Interpret the significance of Peter's vision and the conversion of Cornelius for the inclusion of Gentiles in the church
Explain how the apostles' preaching in Acts centers on their witness to the death and resurrection of Jesus
Explain how persecution scattered believers and carried the gospel into new regions
Compare how Paul shaped his message for a synagogue audience and for Gentile philosophers in Athens
Explain Acts as the second volume of Luke's work and identify its purpose from its prologue
Explain how Peter reads Pentecost as the fulfillment of Joel's prophecy and how it contrasts with Babel
Describe the offices of apostle, elder, and deacon in Acts and explain how the Reformed tradition draws its church order from them
Analyze the accounts of baptism and the breaking of bread in Acts, including household baptisms, and explain how the Reformed confessions use them
Evaluate which events in Acts describe a unique apostolic era and which prescribe practice for the church today
Defend from the text the view that the risen Christ by his Spirit is the primary actor in the growth of the church in Acts
Synthesize how Acts traces the movement from a Jerusalem community of Jewish believers to a church of Jews and Gentiles across the empire

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies, including Pentecost, Acts 1:8, the boldness of Peter, Saul's conversion, the Jerusalem Council, Cornelius, persecution, the timeline, prescriptive vs descriptive, the Spirit as actor, and the synthesis. Fixed the map objective to cover the Roman world and the voyage to Rome. Merged the Jerusalem start with communal life. Added the Ascension, the seven chosen to serve, the Bereans as a practice, Stephen and Philip, the resurrection witness in apostolic preaching, Paul's sermons to different audiences, Luke's purpose, the fulfillment of Joel, church offices, and the sacraments. Anchored the doctrinal objectives to confessions where they state the doctrine. Replaced whole-chapter citations with verse ranges.
